newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GDF, brokerage buy 35pct of Hungary DEGAZ.
newsitem.headline: GDF, brokerage buy 35pct of Hungary DEGAZ.

text.p: Gaz de France and Hungarian brokerage Cashline have bought local council-owned stakes worth a total 35 percent in gas distributor company DEGAZ, a Cashline executive said on Wednesday.
"Cashline Securities has acquired a 19.91 percent share in DEGAZ on behalf of a financial investor," Cashline deputy director Otto Albrecht told Reuters.
The majority owner of DEGAZ, Gaz de France, which bought a 50 percent plus one vote share in the gas distributor at the end of 1995 for $92 million, purchased another 15 percent, Albrecht said.
Albrecht declined to identify the investor Cashline was representing but said it was "Anglo-Saxon"
He said the two stakes were worth a total 4.5 billion forints.
DEGAZ, one of the five regional gas distributor companies privatised at the end of 1995, supplies natural gas to household and industrial consumers in three south Hungarian counties.
DEGAZ has a registered capital of 12.45 billion forints.
